name: Hemoglobin Cooperativity, Allosteric Regulation, 2,3-BPG and the Bohr Effect

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry
clinicalPearls: Tetrameric hemoglobin exhibits positive cooperativity (sigmoidal curve); monomeric myoglobin displays a non-cooperative hyperbolic curve
Oxygen binding transitions hemoglobin from the low-affinity tense (T) state to the high-affinity relaxed (R) state
The Bohr effect right-shifts the curve in acidic, hypercapnic tissues, promoting oxygen unloading to active cells
2,3-BPG nests in the central cavity of the deoxygenated T-state tetramer, stabilizing it and decreasing oxygen affinity
Fetal hemoglobin (alpha2-gamma2) substitutes serine for histidine-143, lowering 2,3-BPG binding and enabling transplacental oxygen uptake
reference.pathophysiology: Hemoglobin quaternary structure coordinates allosteric conformational shifts between T and R states. In metabolically active tissues, protons, carbon dioxide, heat, and 2,3-BPG stabilize ionic salt bridges of the T state, right-shifting the P50 and enhancing peripheral oxygen delivery. In the lungs, high partial pressures of oxygen reverse this binding via the Haldane effect, discharging carbon dioxide.
additionalDifferentials: Carbon monoxide poisoning (left-shift and carboxyhemoglobin elevation)
Methemoglobinemia (Fe3+ oxidation, chocolate cyanosis, unresponsive to supplemental oxygen)
additionalInvestigations: Arterial blood gas with co-oximetry (measures PaO2, SaO2, methemoglobin, and carboxyhemoglobin)
Hemoglobin electrophoresis or high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)
P50 oxygen affinity determination on whole blood
